subject.title: [Bug] Cron Job 使用错误的飞书账号发送消息 - 缺少 accountId 自动推断

question: For cron delivery without `delivery.accountId`, should a configured agent/channel binding outrank a same-channel session `lastAccountId`, or should session-first behavior remain the compatibility default?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve session-first behavior, but the reported multi-account cases show that this can cross account and credential boundaries during scheduled non-interactive delivery.

options.title: Adopt binding-aware precedence
options.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then only safe session/default fallbacks, with fail-closed tests for ambiguity.

options.title: Keep session-first compatibility
options.body: Leave `lastAccountId` precedence intact and document that multi-account cron jobs must set `--account` or stored delivery context explicitly.

options.title: Fail closed on disagreement
options.body: When a cron delivery binding and session-derived account disagree, refuse delivery with a clear diagnostic instead of choosing either account.

recommendation.title: Adopt binding-aware precedence
recommendation.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then only safe session/default fallbacks, with fail-closed tests for ambiguity.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently changed the cron delivery resolver and tests that govern implicit delivery safety.
